literal: In the sixth year he administered Southern Yan Province; soon he was appointed bearer of the staff and governor of Hai Province, but did not take up the post.
idiomatic: In the sixth year he acted as governor of Southern Yan Province; soon he was named bearer of the staff and governor of Hai Province, but never went.

literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to governor of He Prefecture.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he was reassigned as governor of He Prefecture.

literal: Not long after he reached the province, Xiao Gui, Pei Yingqi, and others were defeated and lost in Jiangdong; Mobile Circuit Commissioner Sima Gong set out from Liyang and marched straight back to Shouchun, throwing the border into great alarm.
idiomatic: Hardly had he taken up his post when Xiao Gui and Pei Yingqi met disaster in Jiangdong; Mobile Circuit Commissioner Sima Gong broke from Liyang and fell back on Shouchun, and the frontier shook.

literal: Moreover the province's weapons had been largely exhausted by the army; city walls and watchtowers were badly damaged. Zihui thereupon rebuilt the walls and towers, repaired military equipment, and prepared everything needed for defense; hearts gradually settled.
idiomatic: Weapons in the province had been stripped bare by the retreating army; walls and towers stood in ruins. Zihui rebuilt the fortifications, restored the armory, and made ready every need of defense — and slowly the people steadied.

literal: Soon an edict ordered shipbuilding at the province; Zihui was made grand commissioner to oversee it all.
idiomatic: Soon an edict came to build warships in the province, with Zihui as grand commissioner to oversee the work.

literal: Emperor Wu of Chen once sent his Protector General Xu Du and others with light boats from Zhakou through Dongguan into Chaohu Lake, striking straight at Hefei with the aim of burning the fleet.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen once sent Protector General Xu Du and others in light craft from Zhakou through Dongguan into Chaohu, aiming straight at Hefei to burn the ships at anchor.

literal: At the first watch of night they stole to the foot of the walls; Zihui led officers and soldiers to meet them in battle, and the Chen men fled.
idiomatic: At the first watch of night they crept to the walls; Zihui led his men out to fight them off, and the Chen force broke and ran.

literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to governor of Zheng Province.
idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made governor of Zheng Province.

literal: Zihui was well versed in government and excelled at soothing and settling the people; wherever he governed provinces and commanderies, the place was kept in peace.
idiomatic: Zihui understood the business of rule and had a gift for winning people over; in every province and commandery he held, the land lay quiet.

literal: He was summoned as Left Chief Secretary of the Minister over the Masses and acted as governor of Wei.
idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as left chief secretary of the minister over the masses and acted as governor of Wei.

literal: At the beginning of Ganming he was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture; soon he was formally appointed governor of Wei.
idiomatic: At the start of Ganming he became grand minister of agriculture; soon after he received formal appointment as governor of Wei.

literal: During Huangjian he was additionally made General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: During Huangjian he was further promoted to general of chariots and cavalry.

literal: In the second year of Daning he was promoted to Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: In the second year of Daning he was made minister of justice.

literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled, Zihui was summoned to audience at Zhaoyang Palace.
idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rose in rebellion, Zihui was called to audience in Zhaoyang Palace.

literal: The emperor personally addressed Zihui: "Ji Province lies close to the capital district; Guiyan dares commit such cruel treason.
idiomatic: The emperor spoke to Zihui himself: "Ji Province presses on the capital, and Guiyan has dared such savage treason.

literal: I have already ordered the Grand Marshal, Prince of Pingyuan Duan Xiaoxian, to gather heavy forces and strike like lightning when opportunity appears;
idiomatic: I have already ordered Grand Marshal Duan Xiaoxian, Prince of Pingyuan, to mass heavy troops and strike like lightning when the moment comes;

literal: the Minister of Works, Prince of Dong'an Lou Rui, will command the armies and follow in continuous advance.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Lou Rui, Prince of Dong'an, will lead the armies in unbroken advance behind him.

literal: You bear a family's fame and virtue, and grace extends into that province; therefore I send you to join the military council, and as you find occasion to comfort and settle the people — apply your stratagem well, to fulfill what has been entrusted to you.
idiomatic: Your house has long stood for name and virtue, and the people there know your family's grace. I send you to join the council of war and, as occasion allows, to comfort and settle them. Use your wit well — the trust I place in you must not be wasted.

literal: That very day he took post-horse and rode to the army.
idiomatic: That same day he took relay horses and raced to the army.

literal: Zihui's grandfather had for generations served this province; the common people had long looked to his family.
idiomatic: Zihui's grandfather had held office in this province for generations, and the people had long looked to his house.

literal: Once he arrived, he toured the city and spoke of fortune and ruin; civilians and officials submitted in a stream day and night, and the rebels' every movement, great or small, became known to him.
idiomatic: When he arrived, he walked the walls and spoke plainly of reward and ruin; officials and commoners came over in an unbroken stream, day and night, until he knew the rebels' every move, great or small.

literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was again ordered to act as interim governor.
idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he was ordered to govern the province on interim authority.

literal: Soon he was recalled; ordered to deliberate on law codes with other officials; his rank was raised to Privilege Equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to court to join other officials in drafting law codes, and his rank was raised to privilege equal to the three dukes.

literal: Later the Turks pressed in upon Jinyang; Zihui was ordered to administer Huai Province and took post-horse to the assignment.
idiomatic: Later, when the Turks pressed on Jinyang, Zihui was ordered to administer Huai Province and rode post-horses to the post.

literal: On return he became Minister of the Seven Armies, then Minister of Sacrifices.
idiomatic: On his return he became minister of the seven armies, then minister of sacrifices.

literal: In the third year of Heqing he died suddenly of illness, aged fifty.
idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he died suddenly of illness, aged fifty.

literal: Emperor Wucheng deeply lamented his loss.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng mourned him deeply.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, military affairs of Yan and Ji provinces, governor of Ji Province, opening-establishment privilege, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; posthumous title Jian.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff, military affairs over Yan and Ji provinces, governor of Ji Province, opening-establishment privilege, and right vice director of the imperial secretariat; his posthumous title was Jian.

literal: His son Baogai succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Baogai succeeded him.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was Supervising Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he served as supervising regular attendant.

literal: Zihui's nephew Zixiu, during Wuping, was governor of Bohai and inspector of Huo Prefecture.
idiomatic: Zihui's nephew Zixiu, in the Wuping era, was governor of Bohai and inspector of Huo Prefecture.

literal: When Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan, Zixiu's city fell and he was sent to Yang Province.
idiomatic: When the Chen general Wu Mingche overran Huainan, Zixiu's city fell and he was taken to Yang Province.

literal: After Qi fell he escaped and returned.
idiomatic: After Qi fell, he escaped and made his way home.

literal: In the early Kaihuang era of Sui he died as governor of Tong Prefecture.
idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as governor of Tong Prefecture.

literal: Zixiu was outwardly refined and scholarly, yet bristled with chivalric spirit that could not be crossed.
idiomatic: Zixiu looked the scholar-gentleman, yet carried a chivalrous temper that would brook no slight.

literal: Minister of Works Lou Dingyuan, Zixiu's elder sister's husband, was governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Lou Dingyuan — husband to Zixiu's elder sister — was governor of Yan Province.

literal: Zixiu was in Bohai; Dingyuan came to visit; at a banquet with his wife and daughters his banter was mildly disrespectful; Zixiu flew into rage, beat the drum and gathered troops to attack him.
idiomatic: Zixiu was in Bohai when Dingyuan came calling. At a gathering with Dingyuan's wife and daughters, his jokes turned a little too familiar. Zixiu exploded, beat the drum, and mustered troops to attack him.

literal: In moments troops reached several thousand, with nearly a thousand horses.
idiomatic: Within moments several thousand men had gathered, with nearly a thousand horses.

literal: Dingyuan removed his cap and bowed in apology; only after a long while was he released.
idiomatic: Dingyuan doffed his cap and bowed in abject apology; only after a long while did Zixiu let him go.

literal: Longzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye.
idiomatic: Longzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye.

literal: In youth he was articulate and had talent for practical affairs.
idiomatic: From youth he was quick of tongue and useful in the world.

literal: He first entered office as Supernumerary Gentleman.
idiomatic: He began his career as supernumerary gentleman.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made General of the Central Garrison.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made general of the central garrison.

literal: The Grand Ancestor appointed him Left Grand Master of the Palace for the Grand Eastern Platform, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yancheng County.
idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor made him left grand master of the palace for the grand eastern platform and enfeoffed him viscount of Yancheng County.

literal: He administered Bohai Commandery.
idiomatic: He administered Bohai Commandery.

literal: As area commander he followed Lou Zhao against Fan Zigu; when the affair was settled he was made governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: As area commander he followed Lou Zhao against Fan Zigu; when the campaign ended he was made governor of Qing Province.

literal: Yanzhi loved wealth; in the province he took many bribes.
idiomatic: Yanzhi loved money and took heavy bribes while in office.

literal: Later he administered Jin Province; when the Grand Ancestor returned defeated from Shazhuo, Yanzhi abandoned the province and fled north.
idiomatic: Later he administered Jin Province; when the Grand Ancestor returned defeated from Shazhuo, Yanzhi abandoned his post and fled north.

literal: The Grand Ancestor was furious; all who shared the crime were executed, but for Longzhi's sake Yanzhi alone was spared.
idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor was enraged; all who shared the crime were put to death, but for Longzhi's sake Yanzhi alone was spared.

literal: In the second year of Xinghe he died, aged fifty-four.
idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe he died, aged fifty-four.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, area commander of Ji, Yin, and Ying provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Wengong.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff, area commander over Ji, Yin, and Ying provinces, general of chariots and cavalry, left vice director of the imperial secretariat, minister over the masses, and governor of Ji Province; his posthumous title was Wengong.

literal: His son Xiaozuan succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Xiaozuan succeeded him.

literal: Longzhi's nephew Xiaowan, styled Ziqian; his father Zucao was Chief Clerk of the Northern Pacification Office of Ji Province in Wei.
idiomatic: Longzhi's nephew Xiaowan, styled Ziqian, was the son of Zucao, chief clerk of the northern pacification office of Ji Province under Wei.

literal: For Longzhi's merit in assisting the founding mandate, Zucao was posthumously granted governor of Yong Province and Director of the Palace.
idiomatic: For Longzhi's merit in helping raise the founding cause, Zucao was posthumously granted governor of Yong Province and director of the palace.

literal: Xiaowan was orphaned at seven and was alone among Longzhi's kin to be raised by him, with very deep affection.
idiomatic: Xiaowan lost his father at seven and alone among Longzhi's kin was raised in his house, with a tenderness that ran very deep.

literal: At sixteen the province recruited him as chief clerk.
idiomatic: At sixteen the province recruited him as chief clerk.

literal: In the second year of Yongxi of Wei, Longzhi memorialized to confer upon him his father's enfeoffment as Viscount of Fucheng.
idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi of Wei, Longzhi memorialized to transfer to him his father's title, viscount of Fucheng.

literal: In the third year he took his first office as Military Service Attendant of an Opening Office.
idiomatic: In the third year he took his first office as military service attendant of an opening office.

literal: During Tianping, General of Light Chariots and chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: During Tianping he served as general of light chariots and chief clerk to the minister over the masses.

literal: During Wuding he was chief clerk of Emperor Xiaozong's Opening Office, promoted to Attendant General, serving as Eastern Palace Groom.
idiomatic: During Wuding he was chief clerk of Emperor Xiaozong's opening office, then promoted to attendant general and eastern palace groom.

literal: In the second year of Tianbao he died, aged thirty-six; the emperor heard and sighed in regret.
idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao he died, aged thirty-six; when the emperor heard, he sighed in regret.

literal: Posthumously granted Left General and Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted left general and vice director of the imperial treasury.

literal: Xiaowan was quiet by nature and rather fond of literary composition.
idiomatic: Xiaowan was quiet by nature and loved to write.

literal: Crown Prince Junior Tutor Xing Shao and Minister of the Seven Armies Wang Xin were both senior men of great talent; with Xiaowan they were far apart in age and rank, yet meeting late in life their friendship grew deep.
idiomatic: Crown Prince Junior Tutor Xing Shao and Minister of the Seven Armies Wang Xin were both elder masters of talent; though far from Xiaowan in age and rank, they met late in life and their friendship ran deep.

literal: When Xiaowan's coffin returned home, the two accompanied him to the suburbs, weeping bitterly and moving passersby.
idiomatic: When Xiaowan's coffin went home, the two escorted him to the city outskirts, weeping until passersby turned aside in grief.

literal: At He Shikai's mother's funeral, all who relied on him went to wail.
idiomatic: At He Shikai's mother's funeral, every hanger-on rushed to wail.

literal: Wealthy merchants of Ye such as Ding Zou and Yan Xing all performed filial mourning; one gentleman also wept within the mourning period; Xiaoyan entered to offer condolences and afterward said to others: "South of Yan Xing, north of Ding Zou — there is a court gentleman wailing with extraordinary grief."
idiomatic: Wealthy merchants of Ye — Ding Zou, Yan Xing, and the rest — all made a show of filial grief. One court gentleman wept among them too. Xiaoyan went in to pay respects and, coming out, said: "South of Yan Xing, north of Ding Zou — there's a courtier howling like his heart will break."

literal: Word spread among those who heard.
idiomatic: Those who heard it passed the remark along.

literal: When Shikai learned of it he was greatly enraged.
idiomatic: When Shikai heard, he was furious.

literal: Later when Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Huai memorialized against Prince of Nanyang Chuo for acting arbitrarily, Shikai seized the moment to slander Xiaoyan: "Xiaoyan went out with Chuo, rode his spare horse, left the ranks, and went aside to chat and jest."
idiomatic: Later, when Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Huai accused Prince of Nanyang Chuo of arrogance, Shikai seized the chance to slander Xiaoyan: "Xiaoyan went out with Chuo, rode his spare horse, left the ranks, and wandered off to joke and play."

literal: At that time Xiaoyan's daughter was Princess of Fanyang; using a ceremonial matter as pretext he entered to take leave, and the emperor thereupon had him beaten with a horsewhip over a hundred times.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan's daughter was then Princess of Fanyang; on pretext of a ritual matter he came in to take leave, and the emperor had him horsewhipped more than a hundred strokes.

literal: After he was brought out, Gao Ana'gan was sent to beat him again fifty times, nearly to death.
idiomatic: When they brought him out, Gao Ana'gan was sent to beat him fifty more — nearly to the point of death.

literal: Returning to the capital he held nominal post in the Collection of Documents Office and from then was cast aside.
idiomatic: Back in the capital he kept a hollow post in the Collection of Documents Office and from then on was left in the cold.

literal: After Shikai died he was made Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Dispersal Cavalry.
idiomatic: After Shikai's death he was restored as regular attendant of unimpeded dispersal cavalry.

literal: Later when relations with Zhou were normalized, Zhao Yanshen memorialized about him; an edict appointed him deputy envoy to Zhou.
idiomatic: Later, when relations with Zhou were opened, Zhao Yanshen recommended him, and an edict named him deputy envoy to Zhou.

literal: When Zu Ting took charge of government, he again memorialized to have Xiaoyan enter the Wulin Academy and compile the Imperial Overview.
idiomatic: When Zu Ting took power, he again memorialized to have Xiaoyan enter the Wulin Academy and compile the Imperial Overview.

literal: Xiaoyan's literary skill was not high, yet by elegance he stood apart — skilled at witty conversation, with easy grace in bearing and movement; all admired him.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan's writing was not distinguished, but he carried himself with effortless grace — quick with a jest, elegant in bearing, unhurried in every step — and men admired him for it.

literal: He once said to Zu Ting: "You are a gentleman-minister, unlike the rest."
idiomatic: He once told Zu Ting, "You are a minister in scholar's robes — not like the others."

literal: Those close to power heard and deeply resented it.
idiomatic: Those close to the throne heard and hated him for it.

literal: Soon on his existing office he was additionally made Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his impeachments mostly followed the ruler's wishes.
idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made left assistant director of the imperial secretariat on his existing rank; most of his impeachments followed the ruler's mood.

literal: At that time there was a Buddhist monk named Tanxian who enjoyed the empress dowager's favor; rewards were lavish and his carriages and robes exceeded proper bounds.
idiomatic: At that time a monk named Tanxian enjoyed the empress dowager's favor; gifts poured in on him, and his carriages and robes outran all propriety.

literal: He also petitioned to be Prelate of the Sangha; the Later Sovereign was unwilling, but the empress dowager wanted it, so he received the post — yet the Later Sovereign often resented this.
idiomatic: He also asked to be made prelate of the sangha. The Later Sovereign refused, but the empress dowager wanted it, and Tanxian got the post — though the Later Sovereign never ceased to resent it.

literal: Then monks and nuns brought a lawsuit on other grounds and in their pleading implicated Tanxian.
idiomatic: Then some monks and nuns sued one another on another matter and, in their pleading, named Tanxian.

literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered the offices to investigate.

literal: Xiaoyan judged that he had taken bribes and imposed the ultimate penalty; searching his home they seized great treasures, all confiscated for the state.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan found him guilty of taking bribes and sentenced him to death; a search of his house turned up rare treasures in quantity, all seized for the treasury.

literal: Thereupon he was formally appointed Left Assistant Director and also ordered to present matters at the Gate.
idiomatic: Thereupon he received formal appointment as left assistant director and was also ordered to present business at the Gate.

literal: His nature was rather proud and aloof, not in harmony with the times; as favor rose higher he grew ever more vain — his movements slow and unyielding, bowing to none; discerning men looked down on him.
idiomatic: He was proud and remote by nature, ill-suited to the age; as favor mounted he grew only more vain — slow in movement, stiff in courtesy, bowing to no one — and men of judgment despised him for it.

literal: He died together with Cui Jishu and others for upright remonstrance, aged fifty-one.
idiomatic: He died together with Cui Jishu and others for speaking straight to power, aged fifty-one.

literal: His sons Junque and Junjing, both opening-office military service attendants, were exiled to the northern frontier; his younger sons Junyan and Junzan were castrated.
idiomatic: His sons Junque and Junjing, both opening-office military service attendants, were exiled to the northern frontier; his younger sons Junyan and Junzan were sent to the castration house.

literal: At the defeat at Nan'an, Junque and the other both were executed for association.
idiomatic: At the defeat at Nan'an, Junque and his brother were both executed on account of the affair.

literal: The historian says: The two lords Gao and Feng possessed not an inch of land between them; they raised their arms in Heshuo, intending the royalist cause to avenge Emperor Zhuang — is this not magnificent!
idiomatic: The historian writes: Lords Gao and Feng held not a foot of land between them, yet they raised their arms in Heshuo and meant to march for the throne and avenge Emperor Zhuang — was that not splendid?

literal: Having conquered their native commanderies, they achieved the virtue of yielding — unlike Han Fu, cowed by Yuan Shao's power.
idiomatic: Having taken their home commanderies, they showed the virtue of yielding — not like Han Fu, who cringed before Yuan Shao's might.

literal: Yet their strength fell short of the heroes of the age, their talent was not world-commanding; therefore they welcomed another's banner and abandoned their original design.
idiomatic: Yet their strength could not match the age's strongest men, nor their talent command an era; so they turned to another's banner and set aside their first design.

literal: The Grand Ancestor rode that momentum and so achieved the hegemony.
idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor seized on that momentum and made the hegemony his.

literal: Add to this Ang's courage and strength, his spirit surpassing all things — below Hanling, wind and lightning in his charge.
idiomatic: Then there was Ang's courage and force, a spirit that towered over all — below Hanling he charged like wind and lightning.

literal: Thus the primal merit of the Qi house rested in one clan alone.
idiomatic: So the founding merit of the Qi house stood in one clan alone.

literal: Only they were not Yuan Cong's men of Yingchuan, not the old companions of Fengpei; the trust of heart could not be fully granted.
idiomatic: Yet they were not old companions from Yingchuan, not the men who had followed from Fengpei; the innermost trust could never be given whole.

literal: Exposing their memorials and petitions, using heaven's punishment as proxy — in wrongful excess nothing surpasses this.
idiomatic: To expose their letters and petitions and borrow heaven's wrath for the kill — in injustice, what could exceed this?

literal: Zihui's talent and capacity may be said to have shouldered the family inheritance; generation after generation bearing virtue — this is beauty indeed.
idiomatic: Zihui's talent, at least, was fit to bear the family hall — virtue carried down generation after generation; in that there is true beauty.

literal: Encomium: Fierce and bright the Wen-Zhao spirit, the heroic design made covenant.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Fierce and bright, the Wen-Zhao spirit — the heroic design sealed in covenant.
